mainTopic: פסי ביראות and בורגנין: their limits, and an אגדה on the vastness of the תורה
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא saying that פסי ביראות were permitted only for animals, while a person must climb down into the well to drink. The גמרא challenges this from שמואל, who allows the boards only at a spring-water well, and answers that the water must still be fit for people. רב ענן then asks why the enclosed area must fit a cow's head and most of its body if a person may not hold water before his animal. אביי answers that this ban applies only to a special trough case. Next, רב teaches that בורגנין do not work in בבל and פסי ביראות do not work in חוץ לארץ. An איכא דאמרי version says neither works anywhere outside ארץ ישראל. רב חסדא questions מרי's family walking a long way on שבת, and מרי shows that ruined towns close to one another, not huts, joined the route. The amud ends with אגדה from מרי בר מר: the תורה is 3200 times larger than the whole world. A new דרשה about two baskets of figs begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the quote: a person climbs into the well
steps.stepSummary: This line finishes the ברייתא that the גמרא began quoting on the previous amud. A person must climb down into the well to drink and then climb back up.
steps.simpleTranslation: [But a person] must climb up and climb down.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of a ברייתא that started on the previous amud. It says the boards do not help a person, so a person who wants to drink must climb down into the well and back up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says פסי ביראות were permitted only for animals. A person can manage another way: he can go down into the well itself and drink there. This sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: the corner-boards placed around a well so water may be drawn there on שבת

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new statement. It is the tail end of a ברייתא that began on the previous עמוד: 'The boards were permitted only for animals, but a person...'

phrases.english: climbs up and climbs down.
phrases.notes: The person goes down into the well itself to drink, so he does not need the boards.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְטַפֵּס וְעוֹלֶה מְטַפֵּס וְיוֹרֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא whose quotation began at the end of the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פסי ביראות help only animals. A person must climb down into the well to drink.

steps.title: Challenge from שמואל: boards only for spring-water wells
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that the boards are permitted only for a well of מים חיים. If the boards exist for animals, the type of water should not matter, since animals drink any water.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? Didn't רב יצחק say in the name of רב יהודה in the name of שמואל: the well-boards were permitted only for a well of spring water? If they are for animals, what difference does it make whether the water is spring water or collected water?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the ברייתא's claim that the boards are only for animals. It points to שמואל, who limits the boards to a well with fresh spring water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Collected rainwater (מים מכונסין) is lower quality, but animals drink it without any problem. If the boards existed only for animals, there would be no reason to require spring water. So שמואל's rule seems to show that the boards are really for people.

keyTerms.meaning: collected water, such as rainwater in a pit

phrases.english: Is that so?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב יִצְחָק אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Yitzchak say that Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Well-boards were not permitted
except for a well of spring water alone.
And if [the boards are] for animals,

phrases.aramaic: מָה לִי חַיִּים מָה לִי מְכוּנָּסִין?
phrases.english: what difference is spring water or collected water to me?
phrases.notes: Animals drink either kind.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָאָמַר רַב יִצְחָק אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ברייתא's claim that the boards are only for animals.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that פסי ביראות are permitted only for animals.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל's spring-water requirement only makes sense if the boards serve people. Animals do not care what kind of water they drink.

steps.title: The water must still be fit for people
steps.stepSummary: The boards serve animals, but they are allowed only where the water is something a person could also use.
steps.simpleTranslation: We require something that is fit for a person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Even though the boards are for animals, the leniency applies only where the well holds water good enough for people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer separates two questions: who the boards help, and what kind of well qualifies for them. The boards help animals, but חכמים allowed them only for a well that people also find valuable. This way both the ברייתא and שמואל stand.

phrases.english: We require something that is fit for a person.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעִינַן מִידֵּי דַּחֲזֵי לְאָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא from שמואל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a qualifying condition: the boards serve animals, but only at water fit for people.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the boards are for animals, any water should qualify.
steps.terutzMaskana: The boards are for animals, but only at a well whose water is fit for people, meaning spring water.
steps.whatToRemember: פסי ביראות help animals, but only at a well of מים חיים that is also fit for people.

steps.title: The full ברייתא quoted again with its details
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא and quotes it in full. Boards are for animals only. A person climbs into the well. If the well is too wide to climb, the boards help a person too. A person may not hold water before his animal, but he may pour it out for the animal to drink on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: Well-boards were permitted only for animals, but a person climbs up and climbs down. If the wells were wide, they are permitted even for a person. A person may not fill water and place it before his animal, but he may fill it and pour it before the animal, and it drinks on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: Using the word גופא, the גמרא goes back to the ברייתא it quoted earlier and now reads it in full. This also sets up רב ענן's objection in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two new details appear. First, if the well is too wide to climb into, people may also rely on the boards. Second, a person may not hold a bucket in front of his animal; he may only pour the water into a trough so the animal drinks by itself. The גמרא explains this ban in step 8, where אביי limits it to a special case of a trough that pokes in between the boards.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself': returning to analyze a source quoted earlier
wide, too wide to climb into

phrases.english: The matter itself:
Well-boards were not permitted
except for animals alone,
but a person climbs up
[and] climbs down.
And if they [the wells] were wide,
[they are permitted] even for a person too.
And a person may not fill water
and place it before his animal,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מְמַלֵּא הוּא וְשׁוֹפֵךְ לִפְנֵי בְּהֵמָה
phrases.english: but he may fill and pour out before the animal
and it drinks on its own.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא: לֹא הוּתְּרוּ פַּסֵּי בֵירָאוֹת אֶלָּא לִבְהֵמָה בִּלְבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא from step 1 and quotes it in full in order to analyze it.
steps.confusionAlert: This repetition is on purpose. The word גופא tells you the גמרא is now studying the ברייתא itself, not just using it as a proof.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The boards are for animals. They work for people only if the well is too wide to climb. A person may pour water for his animal but may not hold it in front of the animal.

steps.title: רב ענן: then what good are the boards?
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן objects that if a person cannot even hold water before his animal, the boards seem to accomplish nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ענן objected: If so, what did the well-boards accomplish?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ענן challenges the ברייתא. If a person may not hold the bucket before his animal, it looks as if the boards give no benefit at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ענן's attack is aimed at the restriction on handing water to the animal. He assumes the whole purpose of the boards was to let a person water his animal directly. Without that, the leniency seems empty.

phrases.english: Rav Anan strongly objects to it:

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, מָה הוֹעִילוּ פַּסֵּי בֵירָאוֹת?
phrases.english: If so, what did the well-boards accomplish?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב עָנָן: אִם כֵּן, מָה הוֹעִילוּ פַּסֵּי בֵירָאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ברייתא just quoted in full.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a person may not hold water before his animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the boards do not permit a person to water his animal directly, they seem to have no purpose.

steps.title: Of course they help: they let you draw water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised by the question. The boards clearly help, because they allow a person to draw water from the well at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did they accomplish?! To draw water from them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רב ענן's question with surprise. Without the boards, drawing water from the well would be forbidden, so the boards accomplish a lot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the boards, lifting water from the well into the public area would be forbidden carrying on שבת. The boards make the area count as private, so a person may draw water and pour it into a trough for his animal. The ban on holding the bucket is only a small limit within a real leniency.

phrases.english: What did they accomplish?! To draw water from them!
phrases.notes: He's surprised anyone would ask, because the benefit is obvious.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה הוֹעִילוּ?! לְמַלּאוֹת מֵהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back against רב ענן's objection.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב ענן's claim that the boards are useless.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב ענן overlooked the basic benefit: without the boards, a person could not draw water at all.
steps.whatToRemember: Even with the limit on handing water to the animal, פסי ביראות give a real benefit: they allow drawing water from the well on שבת.

steps.title: Restating the question: why does the cow need so much room?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reframes רב ענן's question. If a person may not hold water in front of his animal, why must the enclosed area fit the cow's head and most of its body?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is the question: what is gained by requiring room for the cow's head and most of its body?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just rejected one version of רב ענן's question. Now it gives the real version. The question is about the required size of the enclosed area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that the area inside the פסין must be big enough for a cow's head and most of its body. That size only makes sense if the cow drinks inside the enclosure. But the ברייתא says a person may not hold the bucket in front of his animal, so the size requirement seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces a corrected version of the question)
What was gained? What purpose does it serve?
Its head and most of its body

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the question that was just rejected in step 6. Step 6 asked whether the boards help at all. This question asks only why the area must be large enough for a cow's head and most of its body.

phrases.english: Rather: what purpose is served by
phrases.notes: The גמרא is fixing how we first read רב ענן's question.

phrases.english: the cow's head and most of its body?
phrases.notes: This refers to the required size of the area enclosed by the פסין.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: מָה הוֹעִיל רֹאשָׁהּ וְרוּבָּהּ שֶׁל פָּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected form of רב ענן's question with a sharper version.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that a person may not hold water in front of his animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The space requirement assumes the cow drinks inside the enclosure. If the cow cannot be given water there, the space requirement serves no purpose.

steps.title: אביי: the case of a trough sticking into the enclosure
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the ban on holding water before the animal applies only in a special case. In that case an אבוס that is a רשות היחיד stands in the רשות הרבים, and its end pokes into the area of the פסין.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: what case are we dealing with here? A feeding trough standing in the public domain. It is ten handbreadths high and four wide, and its end sticks in between the boards.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. Normally a person may give his animal water in any way inside the פסין. The ברייתא's ban covers only one special situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The trough is ten טפחים high and four wide, so it counts as its own רשות היחיד. If it breaks, a person might carry the bucket between domains while fixing it, so the חכמים forbade holding the bucket there. In ordinary cases the cow drinks inside the enclosure, which is why it must be big enough for the cow's head and most of its body.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (narrows a source to a specific case)
Ten טפחים high and four wide (the size of a רשות היחיד)
The upright boards around the well

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer keeps the main היתר broad. Inside the פסין a person may water his animal normally. The restriction is a rare exception.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
With what are we dealing here?
phrases.notes: This is the גמרא's usual way of saying the ברייתא is talking about one specific case.

phrases.english: with a manger standing in the public domain
ten handbreadths high and four wide
phrases.notes: This size makes the trough a רשות היחיד of its own.

phrases.english: and its end goes in between the boards, etc.
phrases.notes: The concern is that if the trough breaks, a person may carry while fixing it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 by limiting the ברייתא to a special case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the ban applies only when a trough that is a רשות היחיד pokes into the enclosure.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that holding water before an animal is always forbidden, which would make the size requirement pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: Normally the animal may drink inside the enclosure, so the area must fit the cow's head and most of its body. The ban applies only in the trough case.

steps.title: רב: no בורגנין in בבל, no פסי ביראות outside ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: A new teaching from רב, reported by רב ירמיה בר אבא. The rule of בורגנין does not apply in בבל, and the היתר of פסי ביראות does not apply in חוץ לארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה בר אבא said in the name of רב: there are no huts in בבל, and no well-boards outside the Land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new teaching about where two leniencies apply. It states the rule first and explains the reasons in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בורגנין are small watchmen's huts outside a city. When they are close together, they count as part of the city, so the תחום שבת is measured from the last hut. רב limits this rule to outside בבל. He also limits the פסי ביראות leniency to ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: Watchmen's huts outside a city that can extend the city for תחום purposes

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said that Rav said:
There are no huts in Babylonia,
phrases.notes: That is, the rule of huts extending the city does not apply there.

phrases.english: and no boards around wells outside the Land.
phrases.notes: That is, the היתר of the boards does not apply there.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב: אֵין בּוּרְגָּנִין בְּבָבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the details of the trough case to the question of where the leniencies apply.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule of בורגנין does not apply in בבל. The היתר of פסי ביראות does not apply in חוץ לארץ.

steps.title: The reasons: floods in בבל and few ישיבות outside ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains both limits. In בבל floods are common, so the huts are not lasting dwellings. Outside ארץ ישראל ישיבות are uncommon, and the boards were allowed only for people traveling to learn תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No huts in בבל, because floods are common there. No well-boards outside the Land, because ישיבות are not common there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason behind each part of רב's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Huts that floods can wash away do not count as real dwellings, so they cannot extend the city. The פסי ביראות leniency was given for עולי רגלים and others traveling for a מצוה such as תורה study. Where ישיבות are rare, the reason for the leniency is missing.

keyTerms.meaning: Yeshiva, a place of Torah study

phrases.english: Huts in Babylonia, no —
because floods are common,
phrases.notes: Huts that can be washed away are not real dwellings.

phrases.english: boards around wells outside the Land, no —
because yeshivos are not common.
phrases.notes: The boards were allowed for people traveling for a מצוה, such as going to learn.

steps.triggerLanguage: בּוּרְגָּנִין בְּבָבֶל לָא — דִּשְׁכִיחִי בִּידְקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasons behind רב's statement in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The huts depend on the place being free of floods. The boards depend on yeshivos being common.

steps.title: In practice we do the reverse
steps.stepSummary: Following the reasons just given, the practice is the reverse. בורגנין work in חוץ לארץ outside בבל, and פסי ביראות work in בבל, where yeshivos are common.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we do the opposite.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes how the halacha works in practice, based on the reasons it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each limit depends on its reason, not on geography as such. Lands outside בבל without floods can use the rule of huts. בבל, full of ישיבות, can use the היתר of the boards.
steps.whatToRemember: רב's limits follow their reasons. Huts fail only where floods are common, and well-boards fail only where ישיבות are rare. So in practice: huts apply outside בבל, and boards apply in בבל.
steps.confusionAlert: "The opposite" does not cancel רב's statement. It applies the opposite rule to the other place: huts in חוץ לארץ, and boards in בבל.

phrases.english: But we do the opposite.
phrases.notes: Huts apply outside the Land, and well-boards apply in Babylonia.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל אִיפְּכָא עָבְדִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical conclusion from the reasons given in step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Huts can extend a city in חוץ לארץ, and the boards are permitted in בבל, because the reasons for each limit do not apply there.

steps.title: A second version of רב's teaching: neither rule works anywhere outside ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: In the איכא דאמרי version, רב ירמיה בר אבא reports in רב's name that בורגנין and פסי ביראות work neither in בבל nor anywhere else in חוץ לארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רב ירמיה בר אבא said in the name of רב: The rules of huts and of well-boards do not apply in בבל, and they do not apply anywhere outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different report of the same teaching of רב from Step 9. In this report, both rules are stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, each rule failed in only one place: huts failed in בבל and boards failed in חוץ לארץ. That is why Step 11 could say each rule still works somewhere. Here, both rules fail in both places, so neither one works anywhere outside ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: Guard huts at a city's edge. When they count as dwellings, they extend the city's תחום שבת.
Corner boards around a well that make the area count as private for drawing water on Shabbos

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the two versions together. In the first version (Steps 9–11), each rule still works somewhere. In this איכא דאמרי version, neither rule works anywhere outside ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: Some say:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said that Rav said:
There are no huts and no well-boards
neither in Babylonia nor outside the Land

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, stricter version of the teaching from Step 9. This version cancels the reversal in Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to this version, neither בורגנין nor פסי ביראות work in בבל or anywhere else in חוץ לארץ.

steps.title: Why huts do not work in Babylonia or anywhere outside the Land
steps.stepSummary: Huts fail in בבל because floods are common there. They fail in the rest of חוץ לארץ because thieves are common there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Huts do not work in בבל, because floods are common there. They also do not work outside ארץ ישראל, because thieves are common there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reasons why huts fail in each place under this version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hut only extends the city if people treat it as a real, lasting dwelling. In בבל, floods wash huts away. Elsewhere, thieves raid them, so people do not live in them steadily. The flood reason matches the first version, while the thieves reason is new and makes the rule fail in all of חוץ לארץ.

phrases.english: Huts in Babylonia do not work
because floods are common;
outside the Land they also do not work
because thieves are common.

steps.triggerLanguage: בּוּרְגָּנִין בְּבָבֶל לֹא — דִּשְׁכִיחִי בִּידְקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the hut half of the ruling in Step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Huts do not count as dwellings where floods (בבל) or thieves (the rest of חוץ לארץ) are common.

steps.title: Why well-boards do not work in Babylonia or anywhere outside the Land
steps.stepSummary: Well-boards fail in בבל because water is easy to find there. They fail in the rest of חוץ לארץ because ישיבות are uncommon there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Well-boards do not work in בבל, because water is common there. They also do not work outside ארץ ישראל, because ישיבות are not common there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reasons why well-boards fail in each place under this version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The boards were a special היתר for travelers, especially people going up to learn תורה, who needed water from a well. In בבל there are rivers and canals everywhere, so no one needs the well, and the היתר is not needed. In the rest of חוץ לארץ, few people travel to ישיבות, so the reason for the היתר is missing there too.
steps.whatToRemember: In the איכא דאמרי version, every place outside ארץ ישראל has a reason against each rule. So neither בורגנין nor פסי ביראות work anywhere in חוץ לארץ.

phrases.english: Well-boards in Babylonia do not work
because water is common.
Outside the Land they also do not work
because yeshivos are not common.

steps.triggerLanguage: פַּסֵּי בֵירָאוֹת בְּבָבֶל לָא — דִּשְׁכִיחִי מַיָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the well-board half of the ruling in Step 12, alongside the hut reasons in Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Well-boards are not allowed where water is plentiful (בבל) or where yeshivos are uncommon (the rest of חוץ לארץ).

steps.title: רב חסדא questions how מרי's family walked three פרסאות on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא asks מרי, grandson of רב ירמיה בר אבא, how his family walks from ברניש to the בית כנסת of דניאל on שבת. That walk seems to rely on huts, yet their own grandfather taught in רב's name that huts do not work in בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to מרי, son of רב הונא, son of רב ירמיה בר אבא: People say that you walk from ברניש to the synagogue of דניאל on שבת, a distance of three פרסאות. What do you rely on? The huts? But your own father's father said in רב's name that huts do not work in בבל!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא challenges a real practice of מרי's family. He points out that it seems to contradict their own grandfather's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Walking three פרסאות on שבת is far beyond the normal תחום, so the city must somehow have been extended. The obvious explanation is the huts on the outskirts. But both versions of רב's teaching agree that huts do not work in בבל, and the person who reported that teaching was מרי's own grandfather.

keyTerms.meaning: Parasangs, a distance unit of about 8,000 אמות each
His father's father, here meaning רב ירמיה בר אבא

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the rule against huts in בבל was treated as binding in practice. A real שבת walk needed a different justification.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said to him,
to Marei, son of Rav Huna,
son of Rav Yirmeya bar Abba:
People say you come from Barnish
to the synagogue of Daniel,
which is three parasangs, on Shabbos.
On what do you rely? On the huts?

phrases.aramaic: הָא אָמַר אֲבוּהּ דַּאֲבוּהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: But your father's father said in the name of Rav:
There are no huts in Babylonia!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי סָמְכִיתוּ — אַבּוּרְגָּנִין? הָא אָמַר אֲבוּהּ דַּאֲבוּהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ruling that huts do not work in בבל, which both versions share, to a real-life practice.
steps.kashyaTarget: The family's practice of walking from ברניש to the בית כנסת of דניאל on Shabbos
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The walk seems to require huts to extend the city. But רב, as quoted by their own grandfather, ruled that huts do not work in בבל.

steps.title: מרי shows a chain of ruined towns within 70⅔ אמות of each other
steps.stepSummary: מרי went out and showed רב חסדא ruined towns that sat within 70⅔ אמות of one another. These ruins, not the huts, joined the whole stretch into one area.
steps.simpleTranslation: מרי went out and showed רב חסדא certain ruined towns that were within seventy אמות and a bit of each other.
steps.whatsHappening: מרי answers the challenge by showing that his family never relied on huts at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Settlements within 70⅔ אמות of each other count as one combined area for תחום שבת. The ruins stood close together in a chain, so the whole route from ברניש to the בית כנסת counted as one connected place. The practice therefore does not contradict רב's ruling against huts in בבל.

keyTerms.meaning: Seventy אמות and a remainder (70⅔ אמות), the distance within which nearby settlements are joined

steps.whatToRemember: The ruling that huts do not count in בבל stands. מרי's family was allowed to walk only because a chain of ruined towns, each within 70⅔ אמות of the next, joined the area together.

phrases.english: He went out and showed him
certain ruined towns
that were absorbed within seventy cubits and a remainder.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפֵק וְאַחְוִי לֵיהּ הָנְהוּ מָתָווֹתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves רב חסדא's challenge in Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual redefinition: the practice relied on a different legal basis than the one assumed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא assumed the long walk depended on the huts extending the city
steps.terutzMaskana: The walk depended on ruined towns within 70⅔ אמות of each other, so the ruling against huts in בבל is untouched

steps.title: Four prophets and the breadth of the Torah
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא quotes מרי בר מר: the idea that the תורה is 'exceedingly broad' was said by דוד, איוב and יחזקאל without explanation, until זכריה בן עדו explained it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: מרי בר מר expounded: What does the verse 'I have seen a limit to every purpose, but Your commandment is exceedingly broad' mean? דוד said this idea but did not explain it. איוב said it but did not explain it. יחזקאל said it but did not explain it. Then זכריה בן עדו came and explained it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new, non-legal (אגדה) section. It lays out a roadmap: three people said the תורה is vast, and a fourth finally explained it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line is a headline that the next steps will fill in. First the גמרא will show the פסוק of each of the three who 'said but did not explain.' The explanation of זכריה comes in steps 21–23. The point is that the תורה is greater than anything else in creation, and each prophet added a piece to this idea.

keyTerms.meaning: Expounded; taught a non-literal interpretation of a פסוק
What is the meaning of what is written? (opens a דרשה)
Your commandment is exceedingly broad (תהלים קיט:צו)
He said it but did not explain it
The prophet זכריה, grandson of עדו, who finally explained the idea

steps.confusionAlert: Do not expect זכריה's explanation here. The גמרא first proves the claims about דוד, איוב and יחזקאל, and זכריה's פסוק comes after that.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
Mari bar Mar expounded:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"To every purpose I have seen a limit;
Your commandment is exceedingly broad"?

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר זֶה אֲמָרוֹ דָּוִד וְלֹא פֵּירְשׁוֹ,
phrases.english: This idea David said, but did not explain it;
Job said it, but did not explain it;
Ezekiel said it, but did not explain it;

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁבָּא זְכַרְיָה בֶּן עִדּוֹ וּפֵירְשׁוֹ.
phrases.english: until Zechariah son of Iddo came and explained it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא, דָּרֵישׁ מָרִי בַּר מָר: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the halachic discussion of huts and well-boards to an אגדה reported by רב חסדא, who also appeared in the previous story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The vastness of the תורה was stated by דוד, איוב and יחזקאל without explanation, and was explained only by זכריה בן עדו.

steps.title: The פסוקים of דוד and איוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows דוד's פסוק and איוב's פסוק. Each says the תורה is vast but gives no exact measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: דוד said it without explaining it, as it says: 'I have seen a limit to every purpose; Your commandment is exceedingly broad.' איוב said it without explaining it, as it says: 'Its measure is longer than the earth and broader than the sea.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins backing up the headline from the last step by quoting the פסוק of דוד, then the פסוק of איוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד only says the תורה is 'very broad,' with no size given. איוב adds a comparison: longer than the land and wider than the sea. Even so, he still gives no real measurement. That is why both count as 'said but did not explain.'

keyTerms.meaning: Its measure is longer than the earth (איוב יא:ט)
As it is written (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: David said it, but did not explain it,
as it is written: "To every purpose I have seen a limit;
Your commandment is exceedingly broad."
Job said it, but did not explain it,
as it is written: "Its measure is longer than the earth
and broader than the sea."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמָרוֹ דָּוִד וְלֹא פֵּירְשׁוֹ, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts filling in the headline of step 17, one person at a time.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד's and איוב's פסוקים describe the תורה as vast without giving a defined measure.

steps.title: יחזקאל's scroll written on both sides
steps.stepSummary: יחזקאל saw a scroll written inside and outside, containing 'קינים, הגה and הי.' This also hints at how much the תורה holds, but gives no measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: יחזקאל said it without explaining it, as it says: 'He spread it before me, and it was written inside and outside, and written on it were lamentations, melody and woe.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the third source, יחזקאל's vision of a scroll packed with writing on both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A scroll written on both sides suggests something holding more than an ordinary scroll can. Again there is no actual size, so יחזקאל too 'did not explain.' The three odd words on the scroll set up the next step, which decodes them.

keyTerms.meaning: He spread it (the scroll) before me (יחזקאל ב:י)
Inside and outside; on both sides
Lamentations, melody and woe: the three words written on the scroll

phrases.english: Ezekiel said it, but did not explain it,
as it is written: "And He spread it before me,
and it was written inside and outside;
and written on it were lamentations, and melody, and woe."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמָרוֹ יְחֶזְקֵאל וְלֹא פֵּירְשׁוֹ, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list from step 18 with the third person, יחזקאל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יחזקאל's scroll, written on both sides, hints at the vast content of the תורה without measuring it.

steps.title: Decoding the three words on יחזקאל's scroll
steps.stepSummary: The three words stand for three ideas. קינים means the suffering of צדיקים in this world. הגה means the reward of צדיקים in עולם הבא. הי means the punishment of רשעים in עולם הבא. Each meaning is supported by a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Lamentations' means the punishment of the righteous in this world, as it says, 'It is a lamentation and they shall lament it.' 'Melody' means the reward of the righteous in the World to Come, as it says, 'to the melody of a lyre.' 'Woe' means the punishment of the wicked in the World to Come, as it says, 'Calamity shall come upon calamity.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to explain the three mysterious words in יחזקאל's scroll. It gives each word a meaning and backs it with another פסוק that uses a similar word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word is matched to a פסוק with a related word. קינים matches קינה, sadness. הגה matches הגיון בכנור, joyful music. הי matches הוה, disaster. Together they cover all of reward and punishment, in this world and the next. This is part of what makes the scroll's content so vast.

keyTerms.meaning: The suffering or punishment of the righteous
In the future to come; עולם הבא
And so it says (introduces a supporting פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: קינים is the suffering of צדיקים in this world. הגה is the reward of צדיקים in עולם הבא. הי is the punishment of רשעים in עולם הבא. זכריה's explanation of how broad the תורה is comes next, in steps 21–23.
steps.confusionAlert: 'קינים' here does not mean lice (as in the מכות). It comes from קינה, a lament.

phrases.english: "Lamentations": this is the punishment of the righteous
in this world,
and so it says: "It is a lamentation and they shall lament it."
"And melody": this is the giving of the reward of the righteous
in the World to Come,
and so it says: "to the melody of a lyre."
"And woe": this is the punishment of the wicked
in the World to Come,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״הֹוָה עַל הֹוָה תָּבֹא״.
phrases.english: and so it says: "Calamity shall come upon calamity."

steps.triggerLanguage: ״קִינִים״ — זוֹ פּוּרְעָנוּתָן שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the three words quoted from יחזקאל's scroll in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קינים is the suffering of צדיקים in this world. הגה is their reward in עולם הבא. הי is the punishment of רשעים in עולם הבא. Each is proven by a פסוק with a related word.

steps.title: זכריה sees a flying scroll with exact measurements
steps.stepSummary: זכריה בן עדו finally explains how big the תורה is. He describes a flying scroll that is 20 אמות long and 10 אמות wide.
steps.simpleTranslation: This lasted until זכריה בן עדו came and explained it, as it says: 'He said to me: What do you see? I said: I see a flying scroll. Its length is twenty אמות and its width is ten אמות.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the explanation that was promised in step 17. זכריה is the first נביא to put actual numbers on the size of the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד, איוב and יחזקאל only said the תורה is vast. זכריה's vision of a scroll, which stands for the תורה, gives real measurements: 20 by 10 אמות. The next step turns these numbers into a full area.

keyTerms.meaning: The נביא זכריה, grandson of עדו
An אמה, a cubit (a unit of length)

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁבָּא זְכַרְיָה בֶּן עִדּוֹ וּפֵירְשׁוֹ,
phrases.english: until Zechariah son of Iddo came and explained it,
phrases.notes: This finishes the sentence begun in step 17: the others did not explain it 'until' זכריה came.

phrases.english: as it is written: 'And he said to me: What do you see?'
And I said: I see a flying scroll;
phrases.notes: 'Flying' suggests it is spread out like two wings, which matters in the next step.

phrases.english: its length is twenty cubits,
and its width is ten cubits.' (זכריה 5:2)

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד שֶׁבָּא זְכַרְיָה בֶּן עִדּוֹ וּפֵירְשׁוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the claim from step 17 that זכריה explained what the earlier נביאים left unexplained.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זכריה's scroll, which represents the תורה, measures 20 by 10 אמות.

steps.title: Opening and peeling the scroll: 40 by 20 אמות
steps.stepSummary: Opened up, the scroll is 20 by 20. Because it is written on both sides, separating the sides gives 40 by 20 אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: When you open it up, it is twenty by twenty. And it is written, 'It was written inside and outside.' When you peel the two sides apart, how big is it? Forty by twenty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא works out the scroll's full area step by step. It uses two clues from the פסוקים to do this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clue one is the word 'flying.' Like a bird's two wings, the 10-אמה width is really folded double, so opened out the scroll is 20 by 20. Clue two comes from יחזקאל's scroll, which was 'written inside and outside.' Counting both written faces doubles the area to 40 by 20, which is 800 square אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: Inside and outside, meaning both sides
You peel it apart, separating the two layers

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק 'written inside and outside' comes from יחזקאל's scroll (step 19), not from זכריה's. The גמרא treats both visions as describing the same scroll of תורה, so it combines them.

phrases.english: And when you spread it open,
phrases.notes: The 10-אמה width was folded like two wings, so opening it doubles the width.

phrases.english: it comes out twenty by twenty.
And it is written: 'It was written inside and outside,'
phrases.notes: From יחזקאל 2:10.

phrases.english: and when you peel it apart,
how much is it? Forty by twenty.
phrases.notes: 40 × 20 = 800 square אמות.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי פָּשְׁטַתְּ לַהּ, הָוְיָא לַהּ עֶשְׂרִין בְּעֶשְׂרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the raw measurements from step 21 and calculates the scroll's total area.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The full area of the scroll is 40 by 20 אמות (800 square אמות).

steps.title: The whole world is 1/3200 of the תורה
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in ישעיה says ה׳ measured the heavens with a זרת. So the world is one square זרת, and the תורה is 3200 times larger.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written, 'Who measured the waters in the hollow of His hand, and measured the heavens with a span...' It follows that the entire world is one part out of 3200 of the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second פסוק so it can compare the size of the world with the size of the תורה. This finishes the calculation and closes the דרשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זרת is half an אמה. So one square זרת is a quarter of one square אמה. The scroll is 800 square אמות, which equals 3200 square זרתות. Since the whole world is just one square זרת, the תורה is 3200 times bigger than the world.

keyTerms.meaning: A span, from thumb to little finger, which is half an אמה

steps.whatToRemember: זכריה's scroll is 40 by 20 אמות, which is 800 square אמות, or 3200 square זרתות. The whole world is one square זרת, so the world is 1/3200 of the תורה. This is how 'the תורה is broader than the sea' finally gets a measurement.

phrases.english: And it is written: 'Who measured the waters in the hollow of His hand,'
phrases.notes: From ישעיה 40:12.

phrases.english: and meted out the heavens with the span, etc.'
phrases.notes: So the whole world is one זרת by one זרת in ה׳'s measure.

phrases.english: It turns out that the entire world
phrases.notes: One square זרת is a quarter of a square אמה, and 800 × 4 = 3200.

phrases.english: is one part in three thousand two hundred of the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִמְצָא כׇּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ אֶחָד מִשְּׁלֹשֶׁת אֲלָפִים וּמָאתַיִם בַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the scroll's area from step 22, together with a new פסוק, to reach the final ratio.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The תורה is 3200 times the size of the entire world.

steps.title: A new דרשה begins: the two baskets of figs
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא quotes another דרשה of מרי בר מר. It is about the פסוק of two baskets of figs set before the היכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: מרי בר מר expounded: What is meant by the פסוק 'And behold, two baskets of figs were set before the היכל of ה׳. One basket had very good figs, like the figs...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new דרשה from the same speakers. This passage stops in the middle of the פסוק, and the explanation comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic, linked to the previous one only because it is another teaching that רב חסדא heard from מרי בר מר. The question 'מאי דכתיב' tells us a deeper explanation of this פסוק from ירמיה 24 is coming. Here we only see the opening words of the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written?
The היכל, the sanctuary of ה׳

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא, דָּרֵישׁ מָרִי בַּר מָר,
phrases.english: And Rav Ḥisda said: Mari bar Mar expounded:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
'And behold, two baskets of figs'
phrases.notes: From ירמיה 24:1-2.

phrases.english: set before the sanctuary of the Lord.

phrases.aramaic: הַדּוּד הָאֶחָד תְּאֵנִים טוֹבוֹת מְאֹד כִּתְאֵנֵי
phrases.english: One basket had very good figs, like the figs
phrases.notes: The פסוק continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא, דָּרֵישׁ מָרִי בַּר מָר, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, separate דרשה from the same chain of speakers (רב חסדא quoting מרי בר מר).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces a new פסוק (two baskets of figs) that מרי בר מר will explain.
